title: Complete parameterization and parameter-space topology of discrete Wigner representations on $d \times d$ phase space
authors: Lucky K. Antonopoulos, Nicolas C. Menicucci
abstract: Toroidal discrete Wigner functions (DWFs) for finite-dimensional systems are non-unique. We classify the labeled single-qudit ${d\times d}$ representations whose phase-point operators are Hermitian, unit-trace, Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal, and Weyl-Heisenberg covariant. Our previously established stencil theorem expresses this family as descents of a doubled ${2d\times2d}$ parent. Here, we solve its projected-stencil admissibility conditions explicitly. In the symplectic-Fourier representation, admissibility fixes the modulus, leaving phase data on a ${d\times d}$ base cell satisfying a parity-dependent twisted-oddness relation. This gives the parameter space ${(S^1)^{(d^2-1)/2}}$ for odd ${d}$ and ${(S^1)^{(d^2-4)/2}\times\mathbb{Z}_2^3}$ for even ${d}$. Canonical horizontal and vertical marginals reduce these spaces to ${(S^1)^{(d-1)^2/2}}$ and ${(S^1)^{d(d-2)/2}\times\mathbb{Z}_2}$, respectively. The same phase data parameterize validity-preserving rephasings of the doubled Weyl-Heisenberg displacement operators. Requiring these operators to have order dividing the Hilbert-space dimension ${d}$ replaces each ${S^1}$ factor by a discrete ${\mathbb{Z}_d}$ factor. The associated symplectic-Fourier characteristic functions encode the same operator information, with pointwise magnitudes independent of the valid stencil convention. This classification separates the freedom intrinsic to DWF validity from that selected by marginal and displacement-algebra requirements and makes explicit the structural distinction between odd and even dimensions.
summary: This theoretical paper classifies the mathematical structure of discrete Wigner representations for qudits by imposing strict physical constraints on their associated phase-point operators. It determines the precise topology of the parameter space, showing how continuous freedom is reduced to discrete factors ($\mathbb{Z}_d$) when additional algebraic constraints are applied. This provides a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding quantum phase-space representations.
main_problem: The paper classifies the labeled single-qudit representations whose phase-point operators satisfy several stringent physical and mathematical criteria.
main_result: The parameter space topology for these valid representations is explicitly determined, yielding specific structures involving circles ($S^1$) or discrete groups ($\mathbb{Z}_d$) depending on the dimension $d$ parity and imposed constraints.
method: The authors use the symplectic-Fourier transform on a doubled lattice space, deriving necessary conditions for validity that constrain the phase data to a specific base-cell structure.

key_observables: The phase data parameterizing the valid PPO frames, the associated DWF, and the symplectic-Fourier characteristic functions.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the qudit, and the constraints imposed by requiring the Weyl-Heisenberg displacement operators to have order dividing $d$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a 'valid' frame satisfying Hermiticity, unit-trace, Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonality, and Weyl-Heisenberg covariance.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the stencil theorem, deriving equivalent symplectic-Fourier criteria, parameterizing the solution via a base-cell phase function, and finally analyzing how imposing additional constraints (like order-d restriction or marginals) reduces the continuous parameter space to discrete or smaller continuous manifolds.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep structural understanding of quantum phase-space representations, which is fundamental for understanding quantum tomography and the mathematical structure underlying quantum measurements in finite dimensions.
